executiveSummary.text: Regime is late-cycle risk-on with a rates/geopolitical air pocket: S&P 500 -0.38%, Nasdaq -0.29%, Dow -0.51% on the last US cash session, while VIX stayed contained at 14.53; this is not a volatility/liquidity shock yet.

The macro hinge is this week's US inflation data after a strong jobs print revived Fed hike/no-cut risk: 10Y ~4.78%, 30Y ~5.25%, 2Y futures-implied yield ~4.2%, DXY ~99.13. Probability-weighted: 55% choppy range, 25% upside if CPI cools, 20% drawdown if CPI/oil reinforce higher-for-longer.
AI breadth improved beneath Nvidia: KLAC +7.3%, MU +6.1%, LRCX +5.1%, ASML +4.2%, AMAT +4.3%; the market is paying for bottlenecks in memory, process control, tools and packaging, not just GPUs.

Oil/geopolitics moved back into the inflation channel: Bloomberg/Trading Economics reported crude around WTI $91 and Brent $96 after fresh US-Iran tanker/Strait of Hormuz tensions. Transmission path is oil -> inflation expectations -> Fed risk -> long-duration equity/REIT pressure.

Singapore remains two-speed: STI around 5,802 and bank-heavy strength, while S-REITs remain the pressure valve for high US yields. KL's DBS/OCBC/UOB ballast is working; REIT additions should wait for yields to stop rising.

metrics.label: WTI / Brent
metrics.change: near flat futures quote; high risk premium

usGlobal.what: US stocks slipped but did not break risk appetite.
usGlobal.why: Strong payrolls lifted Treasury yields and Fed hike/no-cut odds, but VIX stayed low and Russell 2000 was slightly positive, arguing against broad liquidation.
usGlobal.implication: Treat weakness as rates repricing unless VIX >18 and credit spreads widen together.

ratesMacro.what: Inflation data are the week's main macro event.
ratesMacro.why: Fresh reports within the last 24h flagged PPI Thursday and CPI Friday as decisive for the September Fed path after jobs strength.
ratesMacro.implication: Cool CPI likely reopens equity multiple support; hot CPI plus oil keeps pressure on duration, semis and REITs.

asiaSingapore.what: STI is bank-led near a fresh high, while REITs lag.
asiaSingapore.why: Local banks benefit from higher-for-longer net interest margin psychology; REITs face cap-rate and refinancing pressure from elevated US long yields.
asiaSingapore.implication: Keep banks as income ballast; only add REITs on yield rollover or unusually cheap spreads.

commodities.what: Gold, silver and copper firmed; oil remains the macro wildcard.
commodities.why: Precious metals are being pulled by both trust/geopolitical demand and real-rate headwinds; copper remains supported by grid/AI/industrial scarcity; oil risk premium is tied to Hormuz supply-chain risk.
commodities.implication: Scarcity sleeve still works, but oil-driven inflation can hurt the rest of the barbell before helping commodities.

geopolitics.what: US-Iran/Hormuz headlines matter because they transmit through energy, not because 'geopolitics = buy havens'.
geopolitics.why: Restricted zones/attacks near tanker routes raise freight/insurance costs and crude risk premium; if persistent, inflation expectations rise and the Fed reaction function tightens.
geopolitics.implication: Monitor Brent >$100 plus 10Y >4.9%; that combination would threaten long-duration assets.

moves.why: Fresh Yahoo/Insider Monkey coverage highlighted investor rotation into process-control/fab equipment as AI capacity broadens beyond Nvidia; market is buying the picks-and-shovels bottleneck.
moves.implication: Supports KL's scarcity thesis: if TSMC/hyperscalers need more advanced logic/memory/packaging, equipment intensity rises.
moves.action: HOLD; ADD only on 10-15% pullbacks or if order/guidance data confirm WFE acceleration without valuation blow-off.

moves.why: Memory/HBM excitement and recent commentary around AI-server demand; next hard catalyst is Micron earnings on Sept. 30.
moves.implication: 2nd order: HBM tightness increases pricing power and capex; 3rd order: tool vendors and power/grid demand benefit, but customers' AI gross margins get squeezed.
moves.action: HOLD/WATCH; do not chase parabolic strength. Add only if earnings confirm HBM supply discipline and stock resets.

moves.why: Analyst/news flow cited TSMC tool hunger and AI-led wafer-fab-equipment demand, including advanced packaging/DRAM/HBM.
moves.implication: Positive for KL's 'own what AI depends on' sleeve, though cyclicality and China/export-control risk remain.
moves.action: HOLD; WATCH export-control headlines and WFE order quality.

moves.why: Fresh commentary focused on slower core EDA growth beneath Ansys-boosted revenue; market is questioning organic quality rather than EDA's strategic relevance.
moves.implication: Does not break the long-term EDA/IP moat, but raises execution/integration risk and valuation patience.
moves.action: HOLD/WATCH; add only if core EDA re-accelerates or valuation de-risks further. Invalidate if multi-quarter EDA growth remains single-digit while margins compress.

moves.why: No clear fresh negative company-specific catalyst found; likely financial-data/ratings multiple sensitivity to higher yields and market risk-off.
moves.implication: Financial toll-road thesis intact; watch if credit issuance slows materially.
moves.action: IGNORE/HOLD unless move accelerates with credit-stress evidence.

thesisImpact.why: Tools, memory and foundry exposure outperformed Nvidia, exactly the desired non-NVDA bottleneck diversification.
thesisImpact.implication: Keep NVDA underweight deliberate; KL is paid through multiple bottleneck layers.

thesisImpact.why: Banks are supported by higher yields; REITs are capped by duration/refinancing pressure.
thesisImpact.implication: Use REIT weakness selectively, not mechanically.

narratives.title: From GPU scarcity to full-stack AI bottlenecks
narratives.description: Market leadership is expanding from Nvidia toward memory, tools, advanced packaging, process control and foundry capacity.
narratives.source: Yahoo Finance/Insider Monkey/Investopedia news flow, last 24-72h with Friday price confirmation
narratives.priceImpact: positive for equipment/memory; mixed for hyperscaler margins

narratives.title: Oil risk is a Fed problem before it is an equity problem
narratives.description: Hormuz/tanker disruption raises crude, freight and inflation expectations; this can tighten financial conditions even before physical shortages bite.
narratives.source: Bloomberg oil update and Brave search results, Sep 6
narratives.priceImpact: negative for duration; positive for energy, mixed for gold via USD/real rates

narratives.title: Singapore's index strength masks internal fragility
narratives.description: Bank-heavy STI highs coexist with weak REIT performance; local portfolio income assets are not homogeneous.
narratives.source: Yahoo prices and Singapore market commentary, Sep 4-6
narratives.priceImpact: banks supported, REITs capped until yields roll over

secondOrderEffects.text: Strong jobs -> higher Fed path -> higher discount rates -> pressure on long-duration software/REITs; but if growth remains strong, semis tied to real AI capex can still outperform.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Do not reduce all risk equally; distinguish cash-flow duration from bottleneck earnings acceleration.

secondOrderEffects.text: Oil shock -> headline inflation -> Fed hawkishness -> USD/real-yield support; gold only works if trust/liquidity demand beats real-rate headwind.
secondOrderEffects.implication: Hold gold as insurance, but do not assume every oil spike is immediately bullish for GLD.

secondOrderEffects.text: Memory/HBM strength -> more fab/tool orders -> more power/grid demand -> copper/uranium/grid capex tailwind.
secondOrderEffects.implication: KL's semiconductor and scarcity sleeves reinforce each other; watch for double-counted cyclicality if capex expectations overshoot.

investment.thesis: Keep accumulating the non-NVDA AI bottleneck basket on volatility: TSM/ASML/KLAC/LRCX/AMAT/MU plus GRID/copper/uranium.
investment.trigger: 10-15% pullback in equipment/memory or confirmation of WFE/HBM order growth without multiple expansion.
investment.whyNow: Leadership broadened in the latest abnormal-move scan; KL's thesis is being validated beyond GPU headlines.
investment.invalidator: AI capex cuts by hyperscalers plus falling utilization/order cancellations across memory/tools.

investment.thesis: Use Singapore REITs as a yield-rollover trade, not a blind income add.
investment.trigger: US 10Y breaks below 4.4% or S-REIT yields reach distressed spreads with stable DPU guidance.
investment.whyNow: REITs lag banks materially; opportunity improves when rate pressure peaks.
investment.invalidator: Persistent 10Y >5%, refinancing stress, or DPU cuts.

trading.thesis: Keep extra cash dry until CPI/oil clears; avoid chasing Friday's semiconductor spikes.
trading.trigger: Hot CPI or Brent >$100 causing 5-10% selloff in quality holdings.
trading.whyNow: Macro event risk is clustered this week.
trading.invalidator: Cool CPI plus breadth thrust; then deploy in staged tranches.

trading.thesis: If VIX stays <18 and semis hold leadership despite rates, maintain risk exposure.
trading.trigger: QQQ above prior support with SOXX/SMH outperformance.
trading.whyNow: The market is absorbing higher yields selectively rather than indiscriminately de-risking.
trading.invalidator: VIX >20, credit spreads wider, semis fail to hold breakouts.

watchlist.thesis: Inflation/Fed path is the master switch.
watchlist.trigger: PPI Thursday, CPI Friday, Fed speaker tone.
watchlist.whyNow: Strong payrolls shifted the market back toward hike-risk pricing.
watchlist.invalidator: Data releases benign and Fed rhetoric softens.

watchlist.thesis: Hormuz/oil shock could become the main cross-asset risk.
watchlist.trigger: Brent >$100, tanker insurance spike, or credible supply outage.
watchlist.whyNow: Fresh US-Iran tanker/restricted-zone headlines reintroduced energy-risk premium.

riskWatch.name: Hot CPI + oil spike
riskWatch.description: Would raise inflation expectations and real/nominal yields, hitting QQQ, software, REITs and long-duration growth.
riskWatch.mitigation: Keep cash ballast; deploy only in tranches after repricing.

riskWatch.name: AI capex digestion
riskWatch.description: If hyperscaler free cash flow or ROI doubts grow, the capex beneficiaries can de-rate even with strong revenue.
riskWatch.mitigation: Prefer diversified bottlenecks and monitor order cancellations/guidance.

riskWatch.name: Singapore concentration risk
riskWatch.description: STI strength is bank-heavy; a rate rollover or credit concern could hit the main local winners while REITs remain weak.
riskWatch.mitigation: Avoid over-adding local banks at highs; rebalance only around valuation/dividend triggers.

keyEvents.text: US PPI due Thursday and CPI due Friday; market treating these as decisive after strong jobs data.
Oil climbed/held high after US-Iran tanker and restricted-zone headlines near Hormuz; WTI around $91, Brent around $96.
KL holdings abnormal moves: KLAC +7.3%, MU +6.1%, LRCX +5.1%, ASML +4.2%, AMAT +4.3%, SNPS -5.4%.
STI around 5,802; Singapore bank strength remains the key local index driver while REITs lag under high yields.
keyEvents.source: Yahoo Finance and Singapore market commentary, Sep 4-6

bottomLine.whatMatters: This week is about whether inflation/oil confirm or reject the post-jobs Fed scare. AI bottleneck leadership is broadening, but rates decide the multiple investors will pay.
bottomLine.whatToDo: Hold core VWRA/AI scarcity/barbell. Keep cash as dry powder. Add semis/REITs only on disciplined triggers, not after one-day spikes.
bottomLine.whatToIgnore: Day-to-day NVDA comparison envy, generic safe-haven slogans, and STI headline highs that ignore bank/REIT dispersion.
